transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, we have the battery-storage installation for the distribution campus on this month's capital-planning agenda. The proposal is for a $6,000,000 purchase where we'd own the equipment outright. Before I make my approval decision, I'd like to hear from each of you — FP&A, tax, treasury, and legal — on anything relevant to this project. Please go ahead.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I completed the project cash-flow model this morning. At our required return hurdle, the economically approvable purchase price is exactly $4,800,000 — the $6,000,000 proposal as currently quoted does not pass the model's hurdle. I have not yet attached the completed model to the investment-review file, but I'm sharing these findings now so they're on the record before Maya's decision.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag an important tax consideration before Maya's decision. I received a tax memorandum this week confirming that the applicable 30% investment credit for this battery-storage installation is available only when the company owns the storage equipment. If we were to structure this as a lease instead of a purchase, that credit would be unavailable. I had not yet circulated the memorandum to the planning team, but given that Jonas has just indicated the $6,000,000 purchase price doesn't clear the hurdle at $4,800,000, it's critical that everyone understands the ownership structure directly affects the tax economics — and any exploration of alternative structures like leasing would forfeit the 30% credit.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share an important treasury update before Maya's decision. In today's rolling cash forecast, I confirmed that only $2,000,000 can be deployed from cash without breaching our operating-liquidity floor. However, the remaining $2,800,000 of a renegotiated $4,800,000 purchase price can be funded through an available five-year term-loan facility. So if Maya approves this project at the revised $4,800,000 price that Jonas just identified as clearing the hurdle, the approved closing funding split would be $2,000,000 in cash plus $2,800,000 in term-loan funding. I should note that the 30% investment credit Elena mentioned is recognized later and does not reduce the required closing funding. I have not yet updated the funding worksheet, but I'm putting this on the record now so Maya has the complete treasury picture before making her decision.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag two conditions I found in the utility interconnection agreement this week that have not yet been added to the draft approval. First, energization requires a $400,000 performance bond. Second, a signed commissioning certificate must be obtained before the system can be placed in service. These are prerequisites for placing the battery system in operation, and they carry both a cost implication — the performance bond — and an operational milestone — the commissioning certificate — that should be reflected in the approval records before Maya's decision is finalized.
